title: 7 Money Habits That Keep You Broke (And What to Do Instead)

scenes.heading: 7 Habits That Keep You Broke
lines: You work hard. You get paid. And yet, somehow, there's never enough left at the end of the month.
Most of the time, it's not about how much you earn.
It's about a few quiet habits that drain your money without you even noticing.
Today, we're going through seven of them, and exactly what to do instead.

scenes.heading: Habit 1: Spending Before Saving

params.caption: Save first, on payday, before you spend a single dollar

lines: Habit number one is saving whatever is left over.
The problem? There's almost never anything left over.
Flip the order. The day you get paid, move a fixed amount into savings first.
Even ten percent is a great start. Work your way up to twenty.

scenes.heading: Habit 2: Shopping on Autopilot
lines: Habit number two is impulse shopping.
A quick scroll, a flash sale, one click, and it's done.
Try the forty eight hour rule. When you want something that isn't essential, add it to your cart and wait two days.
If you still want it after forty eight hours, buy it without guilt. Most of the time, you won't.

scenes.heading: Habit 3: Lifestyle Creep
lines: Habit number three is called lifestyle creep.
You get a raise, and your spending rises right along with it.
A nicer apartment, a new car payment, more dinners out.
Instead, when your income goes up, keep your lifestyle the same for a while.
Send at least half of every raise straight to your savings and your goals.

scenes.heading: Habit 4: No Budget at All

params.caption: If you don't track it, you can't control it

lines: Habit number four is not having a budget.
Without a plan, your spending quietly becomes bigger than your income.
A budget isn't about restriction. It's about telling your money where to go, instead of wondering where it went.
Start simple. Write down your income, your bills, and a limit for everything else.

scenes.heading: Habit 5: Living on Credit
lines: Habit number five is using credit cards like extra income.
High interest turns a small purchase into a big, long term cost.
Use cards only for what you can pay off in full each month.
And if you already carry a balance, list your debts and pay off the smallest one first, then roll that payment into the next.

scenes.heading: Habit 6: Ignoring Small Wins
lines: Habit number six is thinking small amounts don't matter.
Five dollars a day is over eighteen hundred dollars a year.
Try a simple challenge. Pick a few no spend days each week, and track them on a calendar.
Watching those little wins stack up is one of the best motivators there is.

scenes.heading: Habit 7: Waiting for Someday
lines: And habit number seven is waiting for the perfect time to start.
Someday, when I earn more. Someday, when things calm down.
But time is the most powerful tool your money has. The sooner you start, the more it can grow.
So open that savings account today. Write your budget this week. And automate your savings this month.

scenes.heading: Quick Recap

items: Pay cards in full, count small wins

lines: Let's do a quick recap.
Save first, and wait forty eight hours before buying.
Keep your lifestyle steady when you earn more, and give every dollar a plan.
Pay your cards in full, and celebrate the small wins.
And most importantly, start today, not someday.

scenes.heading: Start Today
lines: You don't need to fix all seven at once. Pick just one and start this week.
If this video helped you, like it and subscribe for more simple ways to build a better life with your money.
Tell me in the comments which habit you're breaking first. See you in the next one.
